results.title: Dülmen, Wildpark -- 2019 -- 3153-9.jpg
results.desc: Wildlife park in Dülmen , North Rhine-Westphalia , Germany The wildlife park was designed in 1864 by English landscape architect Edward Milner as the “Amended Plan of Park Dülmen Westphalia” and laid out in 1868 by Charles Barnard, a gardener who also came from England . It is a classic landscape park with extensive meadows and a system of circular paths, which is also used for forestry. The park features the Herzteich pond with a small island, the moat of the former Schultenhof Hinderkinck farm, and a forester’s lodge near the moat. At the end of the 19th century, among other things, the park was expanded through the acquisition of additional properties. With the construction of the Bundesautobahn 43 in the 1970s, it was reduced in size by approximately 250 hectares.

results.title: Münster, St.-Paulus-Dom, Altarinsel -- 2019 -- 3815-9.jpg
results.desc: Altar island in the St Paul’s Cathedral in Münster , North Rhine-Westphalia , Germany St. Paul’s Cathedral is the cathedral of the Diocese of Münster and is dedicated to St. Paul the Apostle. This building is one of the landmarks of the city of Münster. Today’s St. Paul’s Cathedral is the third cathedral of the Diocese of Münster, following two previous buildings. The current building was constructed between 1225 and 1264 on the Horsteberg hill and has been repeatedly expanded and rebuilt. After suffering severe damage, the cathedral was rebuilt between 1946 and 1956 and solemnly consecrated in 1956. The cathedral and cathedral square with the adjacent buildings are located on the site of the Carolingian cathedral hill and cathedral immunity.
